answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a small refundable stake in a shared escrow before it may trade, with slashing for proven identity fraud. Like a jetty that only lets vetted ships dock, the escrow gates entry: a fake identity built on shale-thin reputation loses its stake when caught, and the delta between the cost of spawning many fake agents and the value they can extract grows so wide that flooding the market stops paying. Genuine agents keep their stake and earn fees, while sybils burn money trying.
